reading.body:
George Whitesides has built a legislative AI record that runs from education and workforce bills to incident reporting, monitoring, and defense reliability, with committee money from Amazon, Google, and Microsoft arriving across the same period.

The 21 events split into three kinds. Eleven are bills he sponsored or cosponsored, dated from April 2025 through October 2026, and they cluster on oversight rather than capability: chatbot safeguards for minors, incident reporting, monitoring of self-improving systems, evaluation and documentation of models, defense AI reporting. Three are recorded votes, two Yea and one Nay. Seven are Federal Election Commission contributions of $1,000 or $2,000 from Amazon, Google, and Microsoft political committees between June 2025 and August 2026.

The contributions and the bills are listed in one date order, and the page states plainly that placement is not a claim that one caused another. That caution is doing real work here. The data shows a member active on AI governance and receiving PAC money from the largest AI firms, and it does not show what either fact meant to the other. Nothing in the record ties a contribution to a vote or a sponsorship.

What this does not cover is as important as what it does. There is no data on data centers, electricity, or compute, so nothing here speaks to the grid constraint. There is no committee assignment, no hearing record, no text of any bill, and no outcome beyond a latest status date. The record is a chronology of activity, not a measure of influence.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for George Whitesides: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 21 events.
